rule: adjusted_score desc, total_score desc; dedupe by arXiv id / URL / id / title

papers.title: Speculative Decoding for Semantic-ID-Based Generative Recommendations
papers.authors: Harshal A. Chaudhari
papers.summary: Generative recommenders that use Semantic IDs represent each item as a short sequence of discrete tokens and usually retrieve several candidates with constrained beam search. That design pays a fixed sequence of model calls on every request. As the generator becomes less sharp, the list can drift from the exact top-K, and the serving system cannot tell when a single request has degraded. SIDECAR first scores an approximate draft with one tree-attention pass and places probability bounds on unexplored prefixes, so it can certify the exact top-K when the draft already contains it. Otherwise it expands only the branches that can still change the output. With a user-sequence draft that contains one interaction, the median request finishes in about 1.7 calls, and about 40% of requests are certified on the first pass. Even when the budget is too small to recover the exact list, it reports a factor around the true ranking, so serving can stop once a quality or latency limit is reached.

papers.title: CACO: Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization for Continuous Generative Retrieval
papers.authors: Pan Zhang, Nan Zhuang, Yongkang Zhang, Kun Xú, Zhongtao Jiang, Zhiwei Wang, Kun Xǔ, Youhuan Li
papers.summary: Continuous generative retrievers sample multiple queries in item embedding space for parallel ANN search, yet independent queries often land in overlapping neighborhoods and waste a fixed budget on duplicate items. CACO attaches a lightweight adjustment network to frozen flow-matching and diffusion backbones, using user history and inter-query interaction to adjust query positions. It uses item retrieval frequency across a reference query pool as a label-free relevance weight where duplicates add no gain. During self-supervised training, it holds other queries fixed and compares opposite perturbations for marginal coverage gain to bypass non-differentiable ANN search. ==Coordinating query positions under a fixed budget improves complementary coverage without changing the backbone or search depth.== Across eight public benchmarks and an in-house streaming industrial dataset, it raises Recall@400 by up to 23.9% over the strongest baseline, cuts inter-query overlap by more than half, adds at most 3.0% inference latency, and works plug-and-play across six frozen backbones.

papers.title: LQ-Rec: Late Quantization for Sequential Recommendation
papers.authors: Satoshi Koide, Yueqi Wang, Julian McAuley
papers.summary: Autoregressive generative recommendation with Semantic IDs faces a structural scaling limit, because longer codes reduce quantization error in principle yet make prediction harder, often degrading ranking quality while inflating encoder memory and decoding cost. LQ-Rec moves quantization to the candidate item side while keeping the sequence encoder and inner-product scoring in continuous space, jointly training the encoder and residual quantizer before freezing the encoder to fine-tune the codebook across every prefix length. ==Because the user vector never reads discrete tokens, model error and quantization error separate additively==, so ranking quality improves monotonically with code length. Across four public benchmarks, it outperforms the non-autoregressive baseline RPG by 19% to 57% in Recall@10 and leads existing Semantic ID baselines on unseen item transitions. At inference time, each query runs the encoder only once, and a single checkpoint can be truncated to shorter prefixes to trade off ranking quality and inference cost without retraining.

papers.title: Towards Realistic Evaluation of Uncertainty Quantification for LLM-Based Recommender Systems
papers.authors: Hao Wu, Sipeng Chen, Weikai Li, Tianyi Chen, Qiancheng Yang, Hang Zhou, Yizhou Sun, Wei Wang, Xiao Luo
papers.summary: When large language models rank items, each request needs a reliable uncertainty monitor, but existing methods draw signals from different sources and apply them at different stages. Some only score an issued ranking, while others use uncertainty to change the ranking itself, so comparisons can mix monitoring quality with reranking effects. A new fixed-ranking benchmark evaluates eight heterogeneous uncertainty signals as record-level monitors under one output contract, across four recommendation datasets and two LLM backbones. Method orderings change with the backbone. Ranking-aligned Top10Mass gives the strongest Error@10 detection under several Llama conditions, but the advantage is uneven: overall AUROC is 0.634 under sparse history and falls to 0.547 on the popularity-tail subset. Scalar signals are also weak at telling whether user history or item text had the larger effect.

papers.title: Needwise: Generation-Free Conversational Recommendation from Need-Level Typed Decisions
papers.authors: Sungchul Kim, Weixiao Huang, Mekala Raja Sekhar Reddy, Amrutha Srinivasan
papers.summary: In conversational recommendation, users add, drop, withdraw, and reverse needs, while catalogs record only some of the attributes. Typical LLM rankers reread the whole dialogue at every turn, which is slow and does not show which needs an item actually meets. The new system maps each turn onto typed decisions over fixed options, then ranks must-first by item type, place, and price. On Google Local, Needwise-HF reaches 0.383 nDCG@10, ahead of GPT-6 Sol at 0.343. Its median response is 2.5 seconds, compared with 5.6 seconds for the latter. The typed state keeps the ranking across topic switches, but it still recognizes only a limited share of withdrawn needs.

papers.title: Learning Generative Ranking Policies for Whole-Page Optimization
papers.authors: Chen Qiu, Zhigang Hua, Qi Xu, Jizhe Zhang, Sha Hua, Ren Mao, Luke Simon
papers.summary: Items on a recommendation page compete for attention and complement one another, so placing the individually best candidates side by side rarely yields the best page. Existing generative re-ranking either assigns one page-level score to every choice, or fits fixed target lists built before training that stop adapting as the generator improves. Given a fixed evaluator, Meta trains the generator in rounds: at each partial page, it places candidates next, lets the current model sample completions, scores each full page, and reweights probabilities into per-position cross-entropy targets. The updated model then builds the next round's data. ==Each position adjusts candidate distributions using complete-page scores==, so serving runs greedy decoding without evaluator search. Under offline referee evaluation on KuaiRand-1K, RL4RS-SeqSlate, and industrial feed logs, it outperforms the evaluated generative recommendation and RL baselines as well as prefix-score beam search, lifting industrial page scores by 13.92% over logged pages compared with the strongest baseline DeGRe at 12.75%. On a synthetic benchmark with known optima, it reaches 97.16% of the optimal score, with its lead coming from page-context contributions.

papers.title: LazUnirec: Unifying Retrieval and Ranking in Multi-scenario Industrial Recommendation
papers.authors: Xiaodong Li, Junfeng Zhang, Shichao Nie, Ziyue Guo, Yiming Liu, Xinxin Xu, Xurong Li, Jinyuan Dang, Zhanming Ou, Jianan ...
papers.summary: Industrial recommenders usually cascade retrieval and ranking as two stages, so their objectives diverge and the user sequence is encoded twice. If the two tasks share one Transformer, conflicting gradients show up in both attention and feed-forward layers, and the model is left without a reliable update direction. LazUnirec keeps both shared and task-private parameters on one backbone, using LoRA-modulated attention and a task-adaptive sparse MoE in the feed-forward layers. When gradients conflict, it uses uncertainty estimates to choose a more reliable direction, then distills knowledge from ranking into retrieval so the two tasks can help each other. Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group has already deployed it in a multi-scenario industrial recommender. An online A/B test ran for one week on ten percent of traffic. In trigger-free scenarios, item page views rose 5.25% and GMV rose 4.01%; in trigger-based scenarios, GMV rose 3.06%.

papers.title: ReAlign: Reward-Guided Preference Alignment for Generative Re-Ranking
papers.authors: YaChen Yan, Liubo Li
papers.summary: Re-ranking should turn an upstream candidate set into the list with the highest user utility, but two-stage generator-evaluator methods split generation from evaluation, so the generator never sees the listwise utility signal. Scoring methods often stay inside the upstream order and never really search the space of permutations. Coupling a decomposable listwise reward model with a candidate-aware autoregressive generator splits the reward by position, models user exposure with a survival function, and estimates heterogeneous engagement such as likes and follows with per-objective heads. The generator is first trained on logged exposure lists, then aligned with within-pool standardized rewards on both the distribution and the ranking. On KuaiRand, NDCG rises from 0.8450 with the strongest baseline, CAVE, to 0.8551. On Avito it rises from 0.7372 to 0.7476. ==Listwise utility steers permutation search toward real engagement only when it is fed back into generation itself==.

papers.title: C3H: Compression-to-Consensus Criteria Hijacking in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems
papers.authors: Guowei Guan, Yurong Hao, Jiaming Zhang, Fuyao Zhang, Wei Yang Bryan Lim
papers.summary: Multimodal LLM recommenders often treat compression and cross-modal fusion as defenses, on the view that compression filters noise and agreement across modalities suppresses anomalies. The same process can also give outsized rank influence to cues that stay salient after compression and are reinforced across modalities, which opens a path for content manipulation. C3H does not query the victim model or poison training. It rewrites a target item's text and image to match the decision criteria the recommender already implies. On VIP5, its ER@20 reaches 1.1 times to 1.8 times the next-best method in every dataset and prompt setting. The same content, transferred unchanged to Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct, leads by 4.7 times on Sports at the high end. Three anomaly-based content filters barely work: exposure shifts by less than 0.004, while utility for ordinary users stays largely intact.

papers.title: SARA: An Auditor-in-the-Loop LLM Recommender for Sustainability Reports
papers.authors: Lars Hillebrand, Thiago B. F. de Oliveira, Tim Dilmaghani, Mohamed Khaled, Writwick Das, Rafet Sifa
papers.summary: Auditing sustainability reports means mapping a checklist drawn from about 1,700 regulatory requirements onto long, repeatedly revised drafts, then judging compliance. The new system is a Word add-in that, for each requirement, recommends the relevant passages and predicts a compliance verdict, while the auditor stays in control. It first predicts a topic and sends only passages from that sub-topic to the language model. On two expert-annotated reports, that is about six times cheaper than feeding the full report to the model, cuts runtime by 42%, and raises precision and F1 by 4.4 and 3.1 points. It is already in production in PwC Germany's sustainability-assurance practice.

papers.title: Deep Cross-Division Network for Product-and-Ratio Feature Interactions in Industrial Ranking
papers.authors: Sofia Gulevskaia, Maksim Utushkin, Aleksandr Poslavsky, Alexander D' Mikhail Trapeznikov, yakonov
papers.summary: Industrial rankers often have to engineer ratio features such as click-through rates by hand, because DCNv2-style cross layers only form polynomial products and cannot represent reciprocal terms directly. Adding a division branch to the cross layer lets the model learn both product and ratio interactions from the same base features, so the entire class of hand-built ratio features can be dropped from the input. In the production ranking stack of a major short-video service, that cut the number of input features by 40.1%. In a live A/B test, likes rose 3.25% and shares rose 16.26%, both statistically significant, while the number of shown videos dipped only slightly. ==Ratios no longer have to be stacked into the input by hand, because the interaction layer can learn the normalized relationships itself==, and model computation time fell as well.

papers.title: GPU-accelerated Multi-relational Parallel Graph Retrieval for Web-scale Recommendations
papers.authors: Zhuoning Guo, Guangxing Chen, Qian Gao, Xiaochao Liao, Jianjia Zheng
papers.summary: Web-scale recommenders must retrieve a small set from a huge catalog in real time, but graph search struggles to put clicks, views, and other behaviors into one relevance score. Under high concurrency, search paths differ from request to request, so traversal often cannot balance breadth and depth, and irregular neural work can stall GPUs. GMP-GR learns a multi-objective user-item metric over those relations, then runs a hierarchical parallel graph search that balances breadth and depth and aggregates irregular computation on GPUs. It is already live in more than twenty Baidu applications, serving hundreds of millions of users and handling more than one hundred billion requests per day. In tests on two recommendation surfaces of the Baidu mobile app, time on page rose 1.13% and 1.19%. Daily active users rose 0.23% and 0.50% on the two surfaces. After system optimizations, query throughput on the two services roughly doubled.

papers.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
papers.authors: Chang Yang, Yao Xuan, Wendan Yan, Nhat Le, Jiang Liu, Longhao Jin, Zhen Peggy Yao, Alireza Vahdatpour, Djordje Gligorije...
papers.summary: Large web platforms run fleets of ads ranking models, and inheriting old features with manual edits struggles to balance per-model serving costs against shared feature pipeline budgets. Meta built a fleet-scale system where LLM agents propose hypotheses and deterministic tools run and verify experiments, finding that ==gains usually come from rebalancing volume across feature categories, since scaling every category up hits diminishing returns==. A shared retrieval LLM, continually fine-tuned on outcomes across the fleet, shortlists cross features before deterministic importance estimators and multi-task Pareto fronts blend the rankings, and a search agent then runs asynchronous trials under serving resource caps. Before training, a trimming step swaps over-budget additions for already-used features of the same category under the same budget. Across production models, it improves NE by 0.31% on average within each model’s budget, trimming cuts pipeline cost by 2.3% on average with no regression beyond measurement noise, and launched models lift a primary online metric by 0.20% in A/B tests.

papers.title: User-Adaptive Fusion of Multiple Foundation Models for Recommender Systems
papers.authors: Sunwoo Kim, Hyunjin Hwang, Geon Lee, Kyungho Kim, Kijung Shin
papers.summary: Naively combining representations from several foundation models often yields only a small gain over one model. The deeper issue is that the users who benefit are not the same for each model, so an average blend rarely helps the people who actually need a particular view. UF2O keeps a separate recommendation view for every foundation model and fuses their scores in a user-adaptive way, so the models need not share one representation space and can even be heterogeneous. The foundation models stay frozen, item representations can be precomputed, and scores from the different views can be computed in parallel. When four foundation models are fused on four datasets, it outperforms existing fusion methods in both static and sequential recommendation, with gains of up to 7% over the strongest fusion baseline. Using four views does not quadruple inference time; the extra cost is less than 60% on average.

papers.title: Weight Coding: Evolving Web-Scale Recommenders through Direct Weight Edits with LLM Agents
papers.authors: Junpeng Hou, Jiaxing Qu, Derek Cheng, Jaewon Yang, Abhinav Naikawadi, Karthik Subbian
papers.summary: Web-scale recommenders usually have to retrain or fine-tune to change behavior, which is expensive and makes it hard to steer exposure for a specific kind of content. Pinterest has an LLM agent edit production weights directly and keep or discard each change with forward evaluation, without backpropagation. On the 147-million-parameter Image Search two-tower retriever, a few edits raised Recall@10 by up to 15 percentage points on evaluation data not used to invent the edits, using about a quarter of the GPU hours of a full post-training fine-tune. In online A/B tests, saves per user from the edited retrieval source rose 8.4% to 10.7%, and the same process can steer exposure toward freshness or products.

papers.title: Multi-Modal Causal Disentanglement for Multi-Domain Sequential Audio Recommendation
papers.authors: Yu Ren, Pengcheng Li, Weijun Xu, Hengzhong Zhou, Shufeng Ye, Qiang Xiao, Dongjing Wang, Chuanjiang Luo, Yong Li
papers.summary: On music platforms, the same user often switches among songs, playlists, and podcasts, with preferences that are coupled yet not the same. Joint training lets high-traffic domains fill the shared parameters and crowd out weaker ones, and item IDs alone rarely connect domains that are semantically close yet share little behavior. CAMAR splits a user representation into a stable cross-domain preference and domain-specific ones, allowing only the stable part to mix across domains, and adds content links with Semantic IDs derived from text, cover images, and audio. For users who have not been active in a domain, a transfer network fills in the missing representation and eases cross-domain cold start. In an online A/B test on NetEase Cloud Music's main-traffic surfaces, the treatment group only added one recall channel on top of the existing per-domain pipeline: play duration rose 1.0% for songs and 1.6% for podcasts, and the playlist like rate rose 3.0%.

papers.title: From Head to Tail: LLM-Augmented Sequential Recommendation and Trade-off Optimization
papers.authors: Adeep Hande, Shaghayegh Agah, Neeraj Sharma, Karina Halevy, Sardar Hamidian
papers.summary: Recommenders often spend exposure on popular items, so long-tail and cold-start items with few interactions are hard to rank well. This work partitions items by interaction frequency, uses an LLM to generate synthetic interactions, and boosts each group's ranking quality and coverage while keeping the drop in overall NDCG@20 within a bound. The best augmentation for each group is not simply additive. On an industrial dataset with a SASRec backbone, group NDCG@20 more than doubled for extreme long-tail items and rose 60% for regular long-tail items; on MovieLens-32M the same two groups improved by 40% and 25%, without a large drop in the overall metric.

papers.title: Intelligent Embedding Pruning for Large-Scale Recommendation Models
papers.authors: Anish Khazane, Alex Saad-Falcon, Guanchu Wu, Marcio Porto, Jasper Shan, Fei Yu, Eugene Shulga, Intaik Park, Yongzhe Zhan...
papers.summary: When training large-scale recommendation models, GPU count is often constrained not by compute, but by sparse embedding tables filling up HBM. Existing in-training embedding pruning (ITEP) dynamically drops less important rows during training, yet usually sets pruning ratios by table size, ignoring feature contributions and sometimes hurting accuracy. Meta's FI-ITEP instead precomputes feature importance, such as by shuffling a feature's values within a batch and measuring the loss change, then assigns higher pruning ratios to less important tables. Across three industry-scale recommendation models, it cuts total memory by 20% to 40% while matching or beating size-based pruning in accuracy, and the same trend holds on the open-source DLRM benchmark. The freed memory lets a frequently retrained model drop from 112 to 80 GPUs with higher per-GPU throughput. ==Larger models carry more low-contribution embeddings, so the compute saved outweighs the upfront estimation cost==; for smaller models with less redundancy, size-based pruning may suffice.

papers.title: From Sessions to Serving: Integrating LLM-Based Embeddings into Retrieval for Production Content Recommendation
papers.authors: Zhixiong Hu, Meng Li, Maggie Zhang, Deborshi Goswami, David Bailey, James Bradley
papers.summary: Autodesk recommends product pages, industry pages, customer stories, and learning content on one site, where standard item-ID sequence encoders drop web events without catalog IDs and running an LLM synchronously breaks latency budgets. LSER keeps the existing two-tower model and sequence encoder, using a fine-tuned LLM to turn raw event text into auxiliary session and history embeddings inside the user tower. Heavy encoding runs asynchronously in a nearline pipeline into an embedding store, so live requests read the stored vectors for ANN search. In offline ablation, adding these LLM features raises popular-product HR@10 by 9.6 percentage points and customer-story HR@1 by 6.0 percentage points, while other surfaces stay essentially flat. The completed online A/B test compared the nearline two-tower stack without the LLM features against the legacy rule engine, lifting product order submission rate by 14.8%, with live testing of the LLM features planned next. ==For sparse multi-content sites, refreshing raw-event LLM features nearline adds semantic signal within retrieval latency limits.==

papers.title: MoR4Rec: Mixture-of-Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
papers.authors: Tiwari Ankit Satyaprakash, Adamya Shyam, Vikas Kumar, Bharti Rana, Venkateswara Rao Kagita
papers.summary: In sequential recommendation, not every interaction in a user history needs the same depth of reasoning, but a typical Transformer still spends the same number of layers on every position. The new method assigns a recursion depth to each interaction, shares a middle block with key-value reuse, and uses gated attention to regulate context. On Amazon Video Games, Industrial and Scientific reviews, and MovieLens 1M, it raises Recall@5, NDCG@5, and MRR@5 by 2.28%, 2.50%, and 2.0% on average over the strongest baseline. In a matched-architecture comparison, it also uses less computation and fewer parameters.

papers.title: OneQuery: Unified Sequence-to-Structure Generation for Multilingual E-commerce Query Understanding
papers.authors: Mingyu Zhang, Jiejie Qin, Jianhui Ji, Rong Xiao, Meishan Zhang, Xiaoyi Zeng
papers.summary: In cross-border e-commerce search, query understanding is often split into language identification, spelling correction, translation, and tagging. Errors in an earlier stage are passed on, the stages are optimized separately, and the pipeline is expensive to maintain. Once a translation is wrong, later tagging often cannot recover. OneQuery folds those four jobs into one schema-constrained generation step, then aligns the model with a three-stage training pipeline and multi-task reinforcement learning. It stays ahead of the staged pipeline across different backbone sizes, which also suggests that domain-specific training on e-commerce queries often matters more than simply making the model larger. Generating the four subtasks together also means four separate modules no longer have to be maintained. In an online experiment on AliExpress search, the list-to-payment conversion rate rose 0.5%, and side-by-side human relevance scores rose 0.8 points, with the gains remaining stable through the trial.

papers.title: ConTra: A Training Framework for Effective Contextual Retrieval via Prefix Generation
papers.authors: Jiajun Hou, Jingbang Chen
papers.summary: To make long documents searchable, systems split them into chunks, and identifying context such as titles or clause numbers is easy to lose once a chunk leaves the source. Context stored only in vectors is invisible to a text reranker, and prompting a large model to write a prefix for every chunk is expensive at index time and not necessarily more accurate. ConTra trains a lightweight model to write a prefix that travels with the chunk, using a reward from frozen embedding and reranking models plus factual checks and a length limit. Each chunk is prefixed once at index time, and the augmented text and its embedding can be reused across queries. On two evaluation collections, the 2-billion-parameter ConTra model leads a prompted 9-billion-parameter baseline and a contextual encoder by up to 3.15 points, and it indexes short documents 7.74 times as fast as the prompted baseline. After post-training on only one collection, it still leads after reranking on another, and it is less sensitive to topically similar distractors.

papers.title: OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval
papers.authors: Zifei Wang, Wei Wen, Qiang Ji, Qian-Wen Zhang, Ruizhi Qiao, He Liu, Xing Sun, Qiang Lin
papers.summary: Multimodal retrieval has to match dense pages, fine-grained entities, ordered video, and agent tools. Single-vector embeddings lose local evidence, cross-encoders reread every recalled item online, and uncompressed late interaction is too large to serve. OmniEVIE is a 4.5-billion-parameter multi-vector model that covers text, images, visual documents, video, and tools with one compressed index and a three-stage retriever. Each record stores at most 128 int8 vectors of dimension 64, about 8.82 GiB per million records, and can locate a hit to a page region or a video interval. On the 190 tasks of MMEB-V3, the full sequence scores 60.68 and the compressed index still scores 60.06, almost no drop. A single-thread query over a million records takes 54.2 milliseconds. Video is encoded directly from frames, without a separate parsing model.

papers.title: PROSPER: LLMs as Sparse Retrievers for First-Stage Product Search
company: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
papers.authors: Hongru Song, Yu-An Liu, Ruqing Zhang, Jiafeng Guo, Maarten de Rijke, Sen Li, Wenjun Peng, Fuyu Lv, Xueqi Cheng
papers.summary: First-stage product search has to reach high recall and still be easy to deploy. Sparse retrieval is interpretable and practical, but short queries and titles often miss each other in the vocabulary; using an LLM as a sparse retriever can also wash out literal signals such as brand names and model identifiers. The new method adds a residual to restore underweighted literal terms and uses a top-k window to sparsify the representation early. On the Multi-CPR e-commerce set, Hit@1000 is 10.2 points above BM25 and also ahead of SPLADE-v2. In a large-scale online A/B test, net GMV rose 1.60%, showing a revenue gain for an industrial hybrid retriever.

papers.title: LARF: Learning-aligned Reasoning Framework for Search Relevance
papers.authors: Tian Tang, Guo Chen, Reed Li, Hao Wang, Yu Lu, Haijin Liang, Haibo Shi
papers.summary: AI-native search has to judge whether a document meets a complex, multi-dimensional information need, and applying a large language model directly is not easy. Ordinary fine-tuning gives little supervision for domain-specific rationales, trajectory-level reinforcement learning may not separate adjacent relevance grades, and chain-of-thought reasoning is often too slow at serving time. LARF first does cold-start fine-tuning on multi-agent chain-of-thought samples, then uses discriminative reinforcement learning with a margin loss on the terminal relevance token, and finally distills the teacher into a student that keeps only classification heads for non-autoregressive inference. On a human-annotated web relevance benchmark with about 300 thousand training and 16 thousand test examples, LARF-8B raises six-class accuracy by 5.78 points and NDCG by 5.05 points. The classification-only serving path cuts inference latency by 82.9%.

papers.title: When Rerankers Work Together: Better and Faster Reranking without Joint Training
company: Southern University of Science and Technology
papers.authors: Yanqiao Chen, Dongsheng Hou, Yuhan Rui
papers.summary: In a multistage retrieval pipeline, how good a reranker is on its own does not tell you how valuable it will be in a cascade. Lexical, single-vector, late-interaction, and precise scorers can be composed without joint training. Two cacheable coarse scorers first learn from passage relevance labels, reuse representations, and run in linear time per item. The comparison holds candidates and budgets fixed, and checks what happens if a stage is removed: whether evidence is kept, repaired, or broken, how accurate the reader stays, and how much online pruning costs. On the long-context NoLiMa setting, inserting them before a CrossEncoder or Provence raises answer accuracy by 4.02 to 9.43 percentage points and speeds up online pruning by up to 1.88 times. Stage-removal comparisons also show an asymmetry: a cascade can beat its final reranker alone, yet still fall short of its coarse selector alone.

papers.title: DiLE: Discrimination-Aware Latent-Space Learning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings
papers.authors: Ben Kang, Junda Wang, Yuxuan Yuan, Hang Li, Yuhan Liu, Xin Chen, Wanting Geng, Tong Lin, Pei Fu, Dong Wang, Jian Luan, H...
papers.summary: Multimodal large language models understand multimodal inputs and task instructions well, yet compressing an input into a single embedding vector does not ensure preserving fine-grained clues such as color or spatial relations to separate relevant items from confusable distractors. The two-stage framework DiLE first guides a few learnable latent queries with a reasoning instruction, combining shared and task-private LoRA experts with auxiliary answer-generation supervision. Stage two periodically refreshes hard negatives retrieved by updated student snapshots and aligns embedding similarities with a frozen reranker teacher distribution via reverse KL divergence. ==At inference, each input is encoded in a single pass into precomputable vectors without the teacher or explicit reasoning traces.== Across configurations spanning two backbone generations, DiLE achieves state-of-the-art overall performance on MMEB-V2, MRMR, and UVRB. With Qwen3-VL-2B on MMEB-V2, it outperforms Embed-RL on the same backbone by 2.8% while running 101x faster.

papers.title: ERA: Embed, Route, Adapt for Cold-Start Cross-Model Latent Retrieval
papers.authors: Venkata Chivukula, Zifeng Wang, Jinsung Yoon
papers.summary: A production retrieval index is tied to the embedding model that built it, so switching the query encoder usually means re-embedding the whole corpus. At cold start there are no query logs, and every document encoded by the new model still incurs compute or API cost. Google spends a small anchor budget on the most informative documents, chosen from the existing target index by cosine farthest-point sampling, trains a lightweight adapter, and uses a deterministic router to escalate the rare hard queries to the target encoder. Across five BEIR datasets, the system matches or outperforms pointwise L2 and embedding-conversion baselines, with relative nDCG@10 gains of up to 35% on Arguana. At a 20% nominal escalation budget, end-to-end query latency falls from roughly 160 ms to 38 to 86 ms, and escalations concentrate on the queries where the projection fails most.

papers.title: When Visually Rich Documents Meet Multi-Vector Retrieval for Region-level Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.authors: Xu Yuan, Liangbo Ning, Yujuan Ding, Qing Li, Wenqi Fan
papers.summary: Vision-based retrieval-augmented generation over visually rich documents often encodes a whole page as one coarse vector and then feeds the full page image to the generator, which can bury local evidence and waste visual tokens. A region-level approach first splits each page into semantically complete regions, retrieves with late-interaction multi-vector matching, and uses those matching scores to estimate each region's contribution so only the relevant regions are rearranged into a compact visual context. Across five benchmarks, it raises average nDCG@5 by 3.47 points over VDocRAG, the strongest single-vector visual baseline, when both use Phi3V. Region-level augmentation also cuts visual tokens by 43% to 62% relative to feeding the full page. Semantically complete regions can serve as a shared basis for matching and evidence selection, keeping retrieval and generation quality with less visual input. Table-style numeric questions can still suffer when headers are cropped away from their values.

papers.title: SOARS: System One Assisted Reranking for Agentic Search
papers.authors: Amin Bigdeli, Liye Fu, Fattane Zarrinkalam, Joel Stremmel, Elizabeth Lingg
papers.summary: Deep search agents retrieve and reason over many steps, and the relevance of the evidence shapes later answers, but calling a reranker throughout the trajectory adds substantial latency and cost. SOARS needs no extra training. It uses a faster System One model for calibrated relevance estimates. At each step, a single call selects query-relevant passages from long documents and reranks candidates, taking into account both the original question and the agent's sub-query. Across six LLM backbones on BrowseComp-Plus and WebShaper, it raises answer accuracy and evidence recall while cutting search calls, end-to-end latency, and inference cost. On BrowseComp-Plus, GPT-5.4 Mini's accuracy rises from 73.9% to 84.7%. Search calls fall from 23 to 14. In other words, deep search need not call an expensive reranker at every step; a calibrated fast estimate can already cut how often it searches and what it spends.

papers.title: Generalized Tensor Parallelism: Powering Trillion-Parameter LLM Training at 10+ EFLOP/s
papers.authors: Shiqing Fan, Deepak Narayanan, Jimmy Zhang, Jiangfei Duan, Prajwal Singhania, Haoran Zhang, Wanying Wang, Philip Monk, X...
papers.summary: Pretraining trillion-parameter language models usually forces a tradeoff between per-GPU memory and throughput. Data parallelism replicates parameters, tensor parallelism and FSDP add communication on every microbatch, and pipeline parallelism leaves GPUs idle while the pipeline fills and drains. For linear layers, these five common schemes are special cases of one framework, generalized tensor parallelism, in which parameters and activations are partitioned and can be gathered back just before use. A parameter gather becomes an optional step before each matrix multiplication, rather than a prelude to a whole Transformer block, so communication can start early without holding memory for too long. On 12,288 GB300 GPUs, an internal two-trillion-parameter MoE model reaches 13.0 exaFLOP per second. Weak-scaling efficiency is 98% from 4,096 GPUs to that scale. The implementation ships in Megatron-Core and can also run million-token sequences on a few hundred GPUs.

papers.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
papers.authors: Jinbin Luo, Xiaozhe Yao, Shang Yang, Zhijian Liu, Song Han, Qinghao Hu
papers.summary: In hybrid LLMs, global-attention KV cache grows with both concurrency and context length, while bounded-state cache scales only with concurrency, so fixed GPU memory partitions can leave one pool underused while the other blocks requests. Hierarchical caching like HiCache keeps restored prefixes resident in GPU memory during decode, leaving the high-bandwidth CPU-GPU interconnect largely idle. Built in SGLang, TideCache keeps fixed virtual addresses for each cache subpool and remaps physical GPU pages on demand, shifting capacity across pools without changing cache layouts or attention backends. ==During decode, it uses bounded-state computation intervals to prefetch the next global-attention layer's host prefix into shared GPU slots==, keeping generated KV resident while the scheduler selects resident or streamed execution from request size and queue state. Across seven model and platform configurations on GB300 and GH200, it completes up to 2.04 times as many agent turns as SGLang with HiCache, cuts overall P50 per-token latency by 20% to 59%, and substantially improves agent P50 TTFT.

papers.title: Supercharging XLA-based inference: Announcing the launch of XLA Serving Engine
papers.authors: Oleg Shaldybin, Monica Song
papers.summary: Many teams train models in Python, yet some production environments disallow Python and face interpreter and global interpreter lock overhead, so Google has open-sourced XLA Serving Engine for the OpenXLA ecosystem. It exports JAX models to an XLA SavedModel storing StableHLO computations and Orbax weights, then runs them in a native C++ runtime wrapping PJRT and the XLA compiler, supporting single-host and multi-host serving while preserving training kernel optimizations. In Google's short-request studies, it achieves 2 to 5 times the throughput of the best Python server they could build using a quarter of the memory. Internally, it already serves over 6 million queries per second across YouTube Shorts, Google Ads, Search, and parts of Gemini Omni. ==It is built as a lightweight one-shot inference engine typically for non-LLM models==, while the authors recommend vLLM or SGLang for large autoregressive language models with long contexts, and PyTorch export via TorchTPU is planned.

papers.title: LoomKV: Lossless KV Cache Compression from GPU Memory to SSD for LLM Serving
papers.authors: Wentao Zhu, Ziao Sheng, Peng Deng, Huiqi Hu, Xuan Zhou, Xing Wei, Zhuang Wang
papers.summary: Serving engines offload the KV cache from GPU memory to host DRAM and SSD so multi-turn and agent requests can reuse prefixes, but tight capacity limits concurrency, and lossy compression can change the outputs. LoomKV adds lossless compression without modifying the engine. A calibrated per-head two-level three-bit code stores BF16 KV at 0.71 of its raw size across nine models. Writes leave the original eviction and prefetch path unchanged, and loads decompress straight into scattered GPU pages. On AgentX, when LMCache's LRU policy is at the eviction cliff, tier mode delivers 2.7 times to 3.6 times the goodput of an uncompressed cache. Where raw capacity already holds the working set, compression costs at most 2.2% of throughput, and tier-mode outputs match the uncompressed ones bit for bit. In pool mode, a fused decode kernel reads smaller pages in place, and when the working set already fits it keeps queueing and goodput close to the uncompressed pool.

papers.title: ModelLess: A Serverless System for Multi-Tier LLM Inference on Shared GPUs
papers.authors: Ding Shi, Wei Wu, Jiayuan Chen, Chenghu Yang
papers.summary: LLM inference platforms often pin GPUs to a product, so cards sit idle between bursts while other work waits. ModelLess makes inference serverless: idle instances scale to zero and sleep with their weights in host memory, releasing and waking in seconds, whereas a cold start often takes more than four minutes. Freed GPUs can be lent to lower-priority tiers, each with explicit rules for what it may lose if preempted. Preemption stops admission, durably re-enqueues a request, and only then releases memory. Replaying a week of traces from 1,100 H20 cards that served long-tail online models shows that about 38% of GPU-time could be lent under a coarse latency target and one fixed idle threshold, but only as an idealized upper bound when recovery takes seconds. If a cold start takes 240 seconds, even per-service thresholds leave only 8%.

papers.title: E2E: Efficient Filtered AKNN Search via Adaptive Termination
papers.authors: Wenxuan Xia, Mingyu Yang, Wentao Li, Wei Wang
papers.summary: In filtered approximate nearest neighbor search, graph indexes such as HNSW typically apply a fixed termination rule to every query, causing easy queries to explore far too many nodes. Early-termination models built for plain vector search look only at traversal distances and break down under filters, because ==when attributes and vector distances misalign, nearby nodes may still fail the filter==. During the mandatory early probing phase of graph search, E2E records the filter-matching ratios of visited nodes and queued candidates. It feeds both ratios and distance features into a lightweight LightGBM model to predict each query's computation budget, stopping easy queries early while letting hard ones search longer. In the high-recall regime, compared with Naive HNSW, it runs up to 2.6× faster on Tripclick and reduces distance computations by up to three times on YoutubeAudio, while improving efficiency by up to 1.5× when adapted to the filter-aware index ACORN. Without altering the underlying graph index, offline training on historical query logs cuts redundant traversal on easy filtered queries.

papers.title: SignalCount: Approximate Counts with Structured and Semantic Predicates in Seconds
papers.authors: Matteo Agius-D', Zachary Zelner, Harrison Ju, Rushab Munot Arrigo
papers.summary: Applications often need a count of how many filtered records meet a criterion that only a reader of the text can judge, such as why a patient stopped a drug, and they need that count in seconds before starting a batch pipeline. Prior systems have an expensive model label a sample at query time, so every query waits. The new system calibrates a fast classifier offline from logs of the production judge and does not call that judge at query time. It samples at most a thousand records, then multiplies the average calibrated probability by the exact filtered count. In a multi-tenant production deployment, p99 latency is 3.8 seconds; on tenants held out from fitting, the interval covers the pipeline count in 92% of estimates, though the estimates run about 15% high in aggregate.

papers.title: Fast 4-bit KV-Cache Decoding on Hopper GPUs: Why Existing Kernels Are Slow and How to Fix Them
papers.authors: Jian Zhang
papers.summary: A four-bit KV cache reads about half the bytes of FP8, but Hopper GPUs have no FP4 hardware, so existing kernels have to decode the values in software. On H200, vLLM's NVFP4 path is up to 1.7 times slower than FP8 and uses only a small fraction of memory bandwidth. The new decode kernel overlaps loads with compute and lays the cache out at write time so decoded values can enter the tensor cores from registers. Inside vLLM, on a mid-size Llama 3.1 model at moderate batches, it decodes 1.12 to 1.64 times faster per step than FlashInfer's FP8 path and holds substantially more tokens. On five mid-size models, repeated runs show no significant accuracy difference from BF16 KV.

papers.title: Design Once, Deploy at Scale: Building a Template-Driven ML Ecosystem
papers.authors: Anirudh Agrawal, Djordje Gligorijevic, Yao Xuan, Peggy Yao, Jiang Liu, John Martabano Landy, Rahul Suresh
papers.summary: In a large ranking and retrieval fleet, trying a new technique on every model separately piles engineering time into repeated work. Meta uses a small set of templates that cover the main ranking and retrieval patterns, so a mature change can be designed once and rolled out across models of different sizes. Over the last two years, that cut per-model engineering time by 92%, improved offline model quality by 0.63% on average at neutral serving capacity, and delivered 0.86% cumulative online lift. Models that adopt a mature template also inherit a history of generalized improvements instead of starting from an isolated baseline.

papers.title: Zarc: Exact Nearest Neighbors over a Billion Vectors in Seconds
papers.authors: Dongfang Zhao
papers.summary: Exact nearest-neighbor search usually either scans the whole dataset or falls back to approximate neighbors, and recent half-precision proofs that skip most vectors still expect one GPU to hold the entire set. The new system keeps only the short proof rows in GPU memory and fetches the remaining full vectors from host memory, so it can answer Euclidean, cosine, inner-product, and filtered queries exactly under updates. On four H100 GPUs, it finishes 10,000 exact queries over a billion vectors in 1.1 seconds, instead of five minutes for exhaustive search. On several open language models, retrieving the exact top-10 attention keys is 2.2 to 13.1 times faster than exhaustive search.

papers.title: RESET: One Demonstration, One Verified World, Self-Improved Skills Across Embodiments
papers.authors: Zheng Sun, Zhuo Li, Zhihao Li, Hengyi Sim, Ge Wang, Ziyue Zhu, Mingkai Jia, Fei Chen
papers.summary: LLM coding agents can iteratively improve robot manipulation skills in simulation benchmarks, but real-world tasks offer neither a ready success scorer nor a resettable practice environment. A single real demonstration already specifies scene geometry, the terminal success criterion, and a physical reference trajectory for checking whether the reconstructed world is faithful, all without depending on the source robot's kinematics. RESET rebuilds a contact-rich world and a frozen, read-only criterion from that one demonstration, checks the world by open-loop replay and silhouette consistency, then revises modular task graphs and skill code from per-node failures, and deploys the frozen code with no runtime language-model calls. On eight manipulation tasks, average success on unseen layouts in simulation is 97%, compared with 27% for zero-shot code. The resulting programs run on four real robots and succeed in 80% of 280 trials. Without target-robot demonstrations, a robot with similar arms can reuse most of the skill functions.

papers.title: SkiP: When to Skip and When to Refine for Efficient Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Mingtong Dai, Guanqi Peng, Yongjie Bai, Feng yan, chunjie chen, Lingbo Liu, Liang Lin, Xinyu Wu
papers.summary: Imitation-learning policies often predict future actions at every control step, whether the robot is in predictable free-space motion or in a precise, contact-rich phase, so temporal resolution is treated as fixed. A skip policy partitions demonstrations into key segments that need dense refinement and skip segments with temporally redundant motion, then relabels the behavior-cloning target in a skip segment with the action at the entrance of the next key segment. The same network can leap over redundant steps and refine carefully where it matters, without a learned skip planner. The partition comes from Motion Spectrum Keying, which reads the local frequency structure of trajectory velocities and needs no manual annotation. Across 72 simulated manipulation tasks and three real-robot tasks, executed steps fall by 15% to 40%, while success rates match or improve. Temporal resolution can be controlled in the supervision signal, without a separate hierarchy.

papers.title: Exploratory Midtraining for Robot Policies
papers.authors: Kshitiz, Zheyuan Hu, Robyn Wu, Yizhou Li, Yunchu Zhang, Vattanary Tevy, Kavya Tayal, Shawn Yin, Aykut Onol, Kushal Arora...
papers.summary: Robot policies are mostly trained on human demonstrations of competent behavior, so they often lack the low-level coverage needed for later autonomous improvement. A form of midtraining can add those behaviors, reconnecting difficult states of the robot and the environment to states from which progress is still possible. The data come from adversarial teleoperation: one person reversibly perturbs the environment while another keeps going to completion without resetting, and trajectory segments are relabeled with local outcomes in natural language. In simulation and on three real-robot platforms, the resulting policies scale more favorably with data, generalize better zero-shot, and make better use of extra rollout time than policies trained on standard demonstrations. In a simulated packing setting, success rises from 54.7% with standard demonstrations to 69.7%. With 2.6 hours of this data, success already reaches 60.3%, comparable to twice as many hours of standard demonstrations.

papers.title: NS-VLA: Towards Neuro-Symbolic Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Ziyue Zhu, Shangyang Wu, Shuai Zhao, Zhao ZhiQiu, Jian Zhang, Li Shengjie, Yi Wang, Anh Tuan Luu, Xinliang Zhou, Fang Li...
papers.summary: Vision-language-action models ground natural-language instructions in what the robot sees and then emit actions, but on long-horizon tasks the backbone often cannot see the structure of the instruction, and generalization stays tied to that backbone. A neuro-symbolic approach parses the instruction into a primitive plan tracked by a gated monotone stage pointer, then conditions a chunked policy only on the active sub-instruction. Training first fits the pointer on demonstration segments and then refines the action policy with success-filtered online learning. Even with few demonstrations, it reaches 42.0 on the long-horizon LIBERO-Long suite, 12.7 points above the strongest baseline, and raises real-robot success from 40.0% to 60.0%. Exposing the compositional structure of an instruction lets the policy track stages instead of leaving that work entirely to the backbone.

papers.title: Tacinf: A Unified Tactile Infrastructure for Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Qiwei Wu, Xiangyu Chen, Xin Xiang, Rui Zhang, Yihang Kang, Weiran Chen, Zikang Xie, Yangfan Li, Tao Wang, Xiangzheng Wan...
papers.summary: Force-aware manipulation needs robots to infer contact force from the task and from touch, but they often lack a low-cost, reusable data and evaluation stack. The new modular infrastructure ties together simulation synthesis, a tactile benchmark, vision-tactile-language-action policies, handheld collection with the same gripper used at deployment, and task-aligned sim-to-real evaluation, and a task instruction can also name the desired force. A foundation model fine-tuned only on tactile simulation data transfers zero-shot to different real-robot tasks. When object positions and instances are both randomized, mixing teleoperation, simulation, and handheld data raises mean real-robot success from 20% with teleoperation alone to 60%. Under firm versus gentle instructions, measured grip force also separates as requested.

papers.title: GenPA: Image Generators as Efficient Robot Policies
papers.authors: Zian Deng, Tianyi Zhang, Zilong Zheng, Ziyu Liu, Tao Zhang, Yao Lyu, Shengbo Eben Li
papers.summary: A line of work that adapts visual generation models for robot control still treats future-scene prediction as the central link to action learning, even when those future images are no longer generated at inference time. The instruction following, spatial understanding, and visual imagination acquired in image-generation pretraining can support control directly, without a future-visual-prediction stage. One approach fine-tunes an image generation backbone with a lightweight action-regression adapter and reuses the model's native generative objective for perception co-training. At deployment it needs only a single backbone forward pass and action regression, with no visual generation and no iterative action denoising. Without extra large-scale robot-data pretraining, it reaches 99.10% success on LIBERO and 83.79% on the out-of-distribution LIBERO-Plus benchmark. Under compiled inference, one action chunk takes 20.9 ms on a single H100 GPU.

papers.title: Force2Act: A Force-Aware Visuomotor Policy for Generalizable Compliant Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Keerthi Vasan Murugan, Fangguo Zhao, Jiafei Duan
papers.summary: Contact-rich manipulation requires a robot to regulate the force it applies, not only where it moves. Policies that copy force from demonstrations fail once the interaction needs more force than any demonstration provided. The new method first plans motion and a relative interaction force for an action chunk, then a mixture of force experts regulates the contact at every control step so the hold is kept when contact changes inside the chunk. On a simulation benchmark of five contact-rich tasks, overall success is 93.8%, against 77.0% for the strongest baseline. On a real robot, average success over four tasks is 94.2%, while the baselines reach at most 27.5%.

papers.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
papers.authors: Xiang Fan, Yuheng Wang, Jiayuan Yan, Bohan Fang, Wisdom Oluchi Ikezogwo, Ainaz Eftekhar, Max Argus, Jason Ren, Jiafei Du...
papers.summary: A single policy that controls many kinds of robots must transfer task knowledge and also adapt its behavior to what each robot can do in the current scene. Shared action representations help transfer, but they do not necessarily say how differences in morphology should change the manipulation strategy. OmniAct conditions directly on a kinematic graph of the robot in that scene, including joint positions, motion axes, and their connection to the visual observation. A flow-matching policy then predicts relative joint motions for each node, so it can cover different degrees of freedom and configurations. The authors procedurally design and filter one million physically feasible embodiments, generate trajectories for them in simulation, and train across diverse manipulation tasks. On 2,000 evaluation episodes with held-out embodiments and scenes, success is 63.0%, compared with 17.8% for pi0.5. On the task families used to evaluate GPT-6 Astra, it reaches 64.7%, compared with 41.1% for that model. On a previously unseen real robot, success is nearly twice that of the next-best method.

papers.title: Revisiting Embodied Chain-of-Thought for Generalizable Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Nan Sun, Yuan Zhang, Yongkun Yang, Wentao Zhao, Peiyan Li, Jun Guo, Wenxuan Song, Pengxiang Ding, Runze Suo, Yifei Su, X...
papers.summary: Embodied chain-of-thought aims to connect linguistic reasoning with robot control, but what form that reasoning should take, and how it should be used, has lacked a large-scale test. One study curates the largest embodied chain-of-thought corpus to date, with 978,743 trajectories, and finds that effective traces must ground high-level semantics in concrete linguistic action guidance, such as end-effector motion and image-space trajectories. High-level reasoning alone brings only marginal gains. More importantly, using explicit chain-of-thought as an autoregressive prefix to actions accumulates errors at inference and does not scale reliably. A vision-language-action model is trained with chain-of-thought dropout, then predicts actions directly at inference to bypass that instability. It reaches an 86.9% success rate on LIBERO-Plus and 53.2% on VLABench.

papers.title: EgoLoAF: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from Egocentric Demonstrations with Hand-Object Affordances
papers.authors: Yiming Zeng, Jiangyuxuan Dai, Yuheng Na, Tan Zhu Xuan, Zihan Lin, Xinfang Qi, Shijian Zhang, Chengqi Shi, Yihan Kuang, Z...
papers.summary: Training humanoid vision-language-action models usually depends on costly real-robot teleoperation. Converting egocentric human videos into training data often still requires wearable motion trackers, leaves hand-object cues implicit, and many methods still mix in real-robot teleoperation for post-training. EgoLoAF derives all of its training data from egocentric demonstrations, without wearable trackers and without real-robot teleoperation during post-training, and uses explicit hand-object relations to guide action generation. It estimates torso motion from camera poses, reconstructs both hand trajectories from video, represents hand-object relations by each hand's current pose relative to the object, and injects those cues into the action expert with cross-attention while freezing the vision-language backbone. The authors also release more than one hundred thousand egocentric episodes, spanning a thousand hours and more than a thousand tasks. Across four real-world tasks, the mean task progress score is 73.1, close to 74.4 for teleoperation, and data-collection efficiency improves by about 4.03 times.
